newsitem.title: USA: U.S.-Canada to appoint salmon trouble-shooters.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-Canada to appoint salmon trouble-shooters.

text.p: The United States and Canada agreed on Wednesday to appoint special envoys to discuss how to "reinvigorate" negotiations over Pacific salmon fishing rights that led to a bitter confrontation, Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said.
The two countries also agreed to establish "an early warning communications system" under which U.S. and Canadian officials would stay in daily contact to try to avert such disputes in the future.
Axworthy was speaking to reporters following urgent talks with Deputy Sectretary of State Strobe Talbot.

They met after Canadian fishermen had held an Alaskan ferry captive for three days in Prince Rupert, British Columbia, to back their protest against alleged U.S. overfishing. The blockade was lifted on Monday night.
"We need to lower the temperature of what has been going on...we have to set the proper climate to resolve our differences and get negotiations back on track as soon as possible," Axworthy said.
He told reporters that the two "eminent persons" appointed as trouble shooters would report directly to President Bill Clinton and Prime Minister Jean Chretien.
